screening_decisions.reason: This is a methodological paper describing reporting guidelines for systematic reviews and network meta-analyses. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise interventions for Parkinson's disease.

This is a randomized, single-blind clinical trial evaluating dual-task aquatic exercises in individuals with PD. It compares an experimental group receiving aquatic exercise to a control group, meeting all selection criteria for RCTs comparing physical exercise for adults with PD.

This is a randomized controlled trial assessing progressive resistance exercise (PRE) in PD patients with akinesia and rigidity subtype. It compares PRE to a control group, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a randomized cross-over trial investigating a theory-driven, progressive, highly challenging group exercise program in subjects with PD. It compares active balance exercises to usual care, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a single-blinded randomized trial examining prescribed exercise effects on fatigue in Parkinson's disease. Participants were randomly assigned to a 12-week community exercise program or control group, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a methodological paper presenting a framework for evaluating confidence in network meta-analysis results. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise interventions for Parkinson's disease.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of Nordic walking studies in Parkinson disease, not a primary RCT. While it reviews RCTs, this publication itself is a secondary research synthesis.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two types of physical exercise (rebound therapy vs weight-supported exercises) in patients with PD. It meets all selection criteria for RCTs comparing physical exercise types.

This is a methodological paper introducing the PRISMA reporting guidelines for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise interventions for Parkinson's disease.

This is a randomized controlled trial investigating Baduanjin Qigong (a form of mind-body exercise) in patients with mild to moderate PD. It compares Qigong to a control group doing daily walking, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a randomized control trial evaluating Argentine tango as a physical exercise intervention in patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease. It compares tango classes to a self-directed exercise control group, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a phase 2, multicenter randomized clinical trial comparing high-intensity treadmill exercise, moderate-intensity treadmill exercise, and wait-list control in de novo Parkinson disease patients. It meets all selection criteria.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of water-based exercise studies in Parkinson's disease, not a primary RCT. While it synthesizes RCT evidence, this publication itself is secondary research.

This is a prospective, parallel-group, single-blind randomized clinical trial evaluating multidisciplinary rehabilitation including aerobic and motor-cognitive components in PD patients. It compares the intervention to a control group receiving no rehabilitation, meeting selection criteria.

This is a methodological paper describing the development of the EuroQol health-related quality of life measurement instrument. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise interventions for Parkinson's disease.
This is an epidemiological study and meta-analysis examining sex ratios in Parkinson's disease prevalence and incidence. It is not an RCT investigating physical exercise interventions.

This is a pilot randomized controlled trial investigating high-intensity aerobic training with cycle ergometers and balance training in PD patients. It compares the intervention to a control group, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a pilot, single-blind randomized controlled trial evaluating treadmill training in patients with mild to moderate PD. It compares treadmill training to a control group following a lifestyle program without physical training, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a systematic review with meta-analysis of dance practice studies in Parkinson's disease, not a primary RCT. While it analyzes RCT data, this publication itself is secondary research synthesis.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing task-oriented circuit training combined with aerobic training (TOCT-AT) to aerobic training alone in people with Parkinson's disease. It meets all selection criteria for RCTs comparing physical exercise types.

RCT comparing partial weight supported treadmill training (PWSTT) vs conventional gait training vs control in patients with Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing physical exercise interventions in adults with PD.

This is a psychometric validation study developing the Falls Efficacy Scale in community-living elderly persons, not an RCT of physical exercise in Parkinson\'s disease. Population does not consist of adults with PD.
Randomized controlled pilot study comparing Tango argentino vs Tai Chi in patients with Parkinson\'s disease. Both are physical exercise interventions, meeting selection criteria.
This is a systematic review and network meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Selection criteria require randomized controlled trials only.
Single-blind randomised crossover trial investigating home cueing programme (physiotherapy intervention) in patients with Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria.
Two-center randomized controlled observer-blind crossover study comparing PMR plus visual cueing vs conventional physiotherapy in patients with idiopathic PD. Meets selection criteria.
Methodological paper about detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. Not an RCT of physical exercise in Parkinson\'s disease.
Randomized controlled single-blind trial comparing Nordic Walking vs Walking in patients with Parkinson\'s disease. Both are physical exercise interventions, meeting selection criteria.
Review article updating diagnosis and treatment of Parkinson disease. Not a primary RCT of physical exercise interventions.
Randomized clinical trial evaluating progressive resistance training vs control in patients with Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing physical exercise intervention.
Meta-analysis of physiotherapy interventions in Parkinson\'s disease. Not a primary RCT; selection criteria require individual randomized controlled trials.
Prospective cohort study estimating minimal detectable change of assessment tools (TUG and DGI). Not an RCT of physical exercise intervention.
Randomised controlled clinical trial comparing different attentional focus instructions during balance training in individuals with Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria.

Randomized controlled pilot study comparing water-based (aquatic) exercise vs land-based exercise in people with Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
Randomized trial comparing simplified Tai Chi training plus routine exercise vs routine exercise alone in patients with mild to moderate Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria.

Single-center parallel-group clinical trial (randomized) comparing high-intensity tandem bicycle exercise program vs control in Parkinson\'s disease patients. Meets selection criteria for RCT of physical exercise intervention.
Systematic review examining effects of Tai Chi on physical function and well-being in Parkinson\'s disease. Not a primary RCT; selection criteria require individual randomized controlled trials.

Randomized trial comparing power-based resistance training (PWT) vs control group in patients with mild to moderate Parkinson\'s disease. Meets selection criteria for RCT of physical exercise intervention.

Randomized trial comparing yoga meditation program vs established proprioceptive training program in patients with Parkinson\'s disease. Both are physical exercise/proprioceptive interventions, meeting selection criteria.

Cochrane systematic review of exercise for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Not a primary RCT, and population is general older adults (60+), not specifically Parkinson\'s disease patients.
This is a psychometric validation study developing a questionnaire (PDQ-8), not an RCT of physical exercise intervention. Does not meet the study design criterion.
RCT comparing versatile physiotherapy intervention to control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (physiotherapy), adult PD population.

Cross-sectional observational study examining associations between non-motor symptoms and quality of life. Not an RCT and no exercise intervention. Does not meet study design or intervention criteria.

RCT comparing Health Qigong exercises plus routine medicine to regular medication alone in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (Qigong), adult PD population.

Part Two of this study is an RCT comparing walking training with verbal instructional cues to control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (walking training), adult PD population.

RCT comparing two types of physiotherapy protocols (treadmill training/kinesiotherapy vs conventional physiotherapy) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population.

RCT comparing two different exercise programs (Agility Boot Camp vs treadmill training) in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population.

RCT (feasibility trial) comparing partnered ballroom dancing to control/usual care in adults with PD. Feasibility trials are still RCTs and meet the selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (dance), adult PD population.
This is a network meta-analysis synthesizing data from multiple studies, not a primary RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion for inclusion.
RCT (pilot study) comparing trunk resistance and stretching exercise to control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.
RCT comparing power yoga to control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (yoga), adult PD population.
RCT comparing combined balance and resistance training to balance training only in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population.
RCT comparing leg muscle power training to low intensity sham exercise in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.
RCT comparing Tai Chi exercise to control/placebo groups in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (Tai Chi), adult PD population.
RCT (pilot trial) comparing Sardinian folk dance to usual care in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (dance), adult PD population.
RCT (delayed-start design) comparing early start exercise program to delayed start in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

RCT comparing treadmill training (speed and mixed) to control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (treadmill training), adult PD population.
Consensus statement proposing standard outcome measures for PD. Not an RCT and no exercise intervention. Does not meet study design or intervention criteria.
Review article on epidemiology of PD including prevalence, incidence, risk factors. Not an RCT and no exercise intervention. Does not meet study design or intervention criteria.

RCT comparing intensive rehabilitation including aerobic exercise to no therapy/control in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (aerobic exercise), adult PD population.

RCT (n=20) comparing Nordic Walking program vs Control group in PD patients. Randomized design, physical exercise intervention, appropriate outcomes (UPDRS-III, HY scale, PFS-16, BDI-II, SAS, NMSS). Meets all selection criteria.

Large RCT (n=231) comparing exercise targeting balance, leg strength, and freezing of gait vs usual-care control in PD patients. Randomized design, physical exercise intervention, appropriate outcomes including fall rates and quality of life. Clearly meets selection criteria.

Methodological paper describing statistical methods for checking consistency in mixed treatment comparisons (MTC/network meta-analysis). Not an RCT of physical exercise in PD patients. Discusses back-calculation and node-splitting methods. Does not meet selection criteria.

Randomised pilot study (n=28) comparing immediate vs delayed start of somatosensory focused balance training in early PD patients. Physical exercise intervention (balance training), RCT design with wait-list control, appropriate outcomes (BBS, TUG, mUPDRS). Meets selection criteria.

Measurement validation study determining minimal clinically relevant change (MCRC) for the Freezing of Gait (FOG) score. Intervention was levodopa medication intake, not physical exercise. Study aims to validate an outcome measure, not test an exercise intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.

RCT (n=22) comparing supervised slackline training vs control group in PD patients. Physical exercise intervention (slackline/balance training), randomized design, appropriate outcomes (FOG, Falls Efficacy Scale, CoP). Meets all selection criteria.

Study comparing two different 12-week exercise programs (United Parkinson Foundation program vs upper body karate training) in PD patients. Groups matched for age, sex, and disease stage. Compares physical exercise interventions in PD patients. Conservative approach warrants inclusion pending full-text review.

Methodological paper introducing the concept of 'treatment hierarchy question' in network meta-analysis. Discusses ranking metrics and treatment hierarchies. Not an RCT of physical exercise in PD patients. Does not meet selection criteria.

RCT (n=22) comparing three interventions: strength training, aerobic training, and physiotherapy in PD patients. All are physical exercise/rehabilitation interventions. Randomized design, appropriate outcomes (UPDRS, Senior Fitness Test). Meets selection criteria for comparing different exercise types.

Postal survey study determining minimally important differences (MID) for the PDQ-39 questionnaire dimensions. Not an RCT of physical exercise intervention. Study involved completing questionnaires at baseline and 6-month follow-up without any exercise intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.

Methodological paper comparing two statistical approaches ('reduce dimension' vs 'reduce weights') for handling multi-arm studies in network meta-analysis. Applied to depression systematic review, not PD exercise RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs examining dance interventions in PD. Secondary research article (review), not a primary RCT. Included 16 RCTs with 636 participants. Does not meet selection criteria which require primary RCTs.

Open-label clinical trial studying Pilates method in PD patients. No abstract available, only keywords. Open-label design may not be randomized. Insufficient information from title/abstract to confirm RCT design. Exclusion warranted pending full-text review.

Pilot RCT (n=20) comparing exergaming vs conventional exercise/control group in PD patients. Physical exercise intervention (exergaming), randomized design, appropriate outcomes (Berg Balance Scale, Fatigue Severity Scale, PDQ-39). Meets all selection criteria.

RCT (n=40) comparing water-based exercise vs land-based rehabilitation therapy in PD patients. Both are physical exercise interventions. Randomized design, appropriate outcomes (UPDRS-III, BBS, TUGT, 6MWT, 10MWT). Meets selection criteria for comparing different exercise types.

RCT (n=51) comparing exercise intervention vs usual care (wait-listed) in early/midstage PD patients. Physical exercise intervention focusing on spinal flexibility, randomized design, appropriate outcomes (functional axial rotation, functional reach, timed supine to stand). Meets all selection criteria.

Study comparing Dance Group (Dance for PD classes) vs Control Group (treatment as usual) in early-stage PD patients. Physical exercise intervention (dance), allocated to groups, appropriate outcomes (MDS-UPDRS, NIH Toolbox cognition, HADS, PDQ-39). Meets selection criteria.

Pilot RCT (n=32) comparing immediate gym training vs delayed start (waiting-list control) in mild-moderate PD patients. Physical exercise intervention (gym training), randomized design, appropriate outcomes (reaction time, UPDRS, quality of life). Meets all selection criteria.

RCT (n=41) comparing robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) vs conventional physiotherapy in PD patients. Both are physical rehabilitation/exercise interventions. Randomized design, appropriate outcomes (10-m walking speed, 6-minute walk distance). Meets selection criteria for comparing different exercise/rehabilitation types.

Quasi-randomized pilot trial (n=46) comparing dance vs PD exercise vs non-intervention groups in mild-moderate PD patients. Physical exercise intervention (dance), quasi-randomized design (patient associations randomly assigned), appropriate outcomes (TUG, BBS, FAB, MRT, AS, SDS, UPDRS). Conservative approach warrants inclusion despite quasi-randomization.

This is an RCT comparing the HiBalance program (highly challenging balance training incorporating dual-tasking and PD-specific components) to usual care in elderly with mild to moderate PD. Meets all inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is a pilot RCT examining Hatha yoga intervention versus wait-list control in individuals with PD. Yoga qualifies as physical exercise. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is a randomized study comparing balance and strength training program to control group in persons with stage I-III Parkinsonism. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This study appears to be an observational/comparative study rather than an RCT. It compares four groups (PDBT, HBT, PDNT, HNT) but does not clearly describe randomization. The primary focus is on immunomodulatory effects (cytokines, neurotrophic factors) rather than motor signs, QoL, or adverse events. Does not clearly meet RCT criterion.

This is an RCT comparing group boxing training to traditional group exercise in adults with PD. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, comparing two types of physical exercise, adult PD population.

This is an RCT comparing rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) gait training to self-paced training and no-training control groups in PD patients. Gait training with RAS qualifies as physical exercise intervention. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is a clinico-pathological study examining diagnostic accuracy, not an RCT. No intervention is tested; it retrospectively analyzes pathological findings in 100 patients diagnosed with PD. Does not meet RCT criterion or involve physical exercise intervention.

This is an RCT comparing a physical therapy program (stretching and flexibility exercises emphasizing balance and gait) to control group in patients with moderate PD. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is a cross-sectional analysis determining clinically important differences (CIDs) for the UPDRS scale. It is not an RCT and does not test any physical exercise intervention. It is a measurement/validation study. Does not meet RCT criterion.

This is an RCT comparing tai chi to resistance training and stretching in 195 patients with idiopathic PD (stage 1-4). All three are physical exercise interventions. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, comparing multiple types of physical exercise, adult PD population.

This is an RCT comparing sensory attention focused exercise (PD SAFEx) and lower-limb aerobic training to non-exercise control group in PD patients. Both interventions qualify as physical exercise. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population.

This is an epidemiological incidence study of PSP and MSA, not an RCT. No intervention is tested; it examines disease incidence rates over time. Does not meet RCT criterion or involve physical exercise intervention.

This is an RCT comparing tango classes to exercise classes in 19 subjects with PD. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, comparing two types of physical exercise, adult PD population.

This is a pilot RCT comparing resistance training (leg press, leg curl, calf press) to standard care in 18 persons with PD. Resistance training qualifies as physical exercise. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is an RCT comparing audio-visual cued task-specific training to conventional exercise and no treatment control in 52 subjects with PD. Both interventions involve physical activity/exercise components. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population.

This is a pragmatic RCT comparing a physiotherapy-led strength and balance training programme to usual care in 130 people with PD who have a history of falls. Strength and balance training qualifies as physical exercise. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is an RCT comparing high-intensity sensorimotor agility exercise with maintenance (E+M) to exercise only (E) and no exercise control (C) over 2 years. Agility training qualifies as physical exercise. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is an RCT comparing agility exergaming (EXE) to stationary cycling (CYC) and wait-listed control in 74 PD patients. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, comparing two types of physical exercise, adult PD population.

This is an RCT comparing intensive physical therapy program to no specific intervention (control) in 40 PD patients with mild cognitive impairment. Physical therapy includes physical exercise components. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

This is a single-blind pilot RCT comparing Halliwick style aquatic physiotherapy to traditional aquatic and land-based physiotherapy in 30 participants with moderate PD. Aquatic physiotherapy qualifies as physical exercise. Meets inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Study is a feasibility/pilot trial but meets core criteria. Conservative inclusion recommended.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
Abstract is truncated/incomplete (only shows background). Cannot rule out that this is an RCT comparing exercise interventions for adults with PD. Conservative inclusion recommended.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Study is a feasibility/pilot trial but meets core criteria. Conservative inclusion recommended.
Animal study (rats), not human participants with PD. Selection criteria require RCTs in adults with PD.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Study is a feasibility/pilot trial but meets core criteria. Conservative inclusion recommended.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis or epidemiological study, not a primary RCT. Selection criteria require individual RCTs.
RCT comparing physical exercise intervention(s) for adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a systematic review of 43 trials, not a primary RCT. The selection criteria require randomized controlled trials, not review articles.
This is a basic science animal study using in vivo striatal recordings in mice. It does not involve human participants with PD, nor is it an RCT of physical exercise.
This is a methodological paper about network meta-analysis techniques. It is not an RCT and does not involve PD patients or physical exercise interventions.
This is a mixed methods study exploring participants' perceptions about exercise. While it references an RCT, the study itself is qualitative (interviews) and not an RCT of physical exercise.
This is a methodological paper developing a taxonomy for fall-prevention interventions. It is not an RCT and does not involve PD patients.

This is an RCT with 68 subjects with PD comparing physical therapy + medication vs. medication only. It meets all selection criteria: RCT design, PD population, physical exercise intervention, and control comparison.
This is an RCT comparing yoga intervention (n=13) to control group (n=13) in people with PD. Yoga is a form of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about imputing standard deviations in meta-analyses. It is not an RCT and does not involve PD patients or physical exercise.

This is a randomized feasibility study (n=18) comparing RGRM Method to control in PD patients. The intervention involves rhythm and music which includes physical components. Being conservative, this is included as it is a randomized study with PD patients and an intervention.
This is an epidemiological study about incidence and mortality of parkinsonism. It is not an RCT and does not involve physical exercise interventions.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The selection criteria require randomized controlled trials.
This is an RCT (n=18) comparing progressive resistance training to non-contact control in individuals with PD. PRT is a form of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT (n=70) comparing brisk walking and balance exercise to active control (upper limb training) in people with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a feature review article integrating animal and human research. It is not an RCT.

This is an RCT (n=86) comparing rhythmic auditory stimulation + intensive muscle strength training to rhythmic auditory stimulation alone in elderly PD patients. The intervention includes physical exercise (muscle strength training). Meets selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing movement strategy training to musculoskeletal exercises in hospitalized PD patients. Both interventions involve physical components. Meets selection criteria.
This is an RCT (n=26) comparing aerobic exercise to non-exercising control in persons with early PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review/seminal article about Parkinson's disease. It is not an RCT and does not involve physical exercise interventions.
This is an RCT (n=33) comparing downhill walking training to conventional therapy in PD patients. Downhill walking is a form of physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT (n=28) comparing VR training to conventional physical therapy in PD patients. Both interventions involve physical exercise components. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a questionnaire development and validation study, not an RCT. It involves postal surveys and clinic surveys to validate the PDQ-39 measure. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested.

This is a questionnaire development study for assessing freezing of gait. It is not an RCT and does not involve any physical exercise intervention. The study only administers questionnaires to assess reliability.

This is an RCT where 40 PD patients were randomized to tai chi (n=20) or multimodal exercise training (n=20). Both are physical exercise interventions being compared in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an instrument development study for measuring balance in elderly individuals (ages 60-93), not specifically PD patients. It is not an RCT and does not involve any exercise intervention.
This is a longitudinal observational study examining health economic burden in PD patients. It is not an RCT and does not involve any physical exercise intervention.
This is a test validation study for frail elderly persons (mean age 79.5 years), not specifically PD patients. It is not an RCT and does not involve any exercise intervention.

This is an RCT where 40 PD patients were randomly assigned to resistance training or balance training (both physical exercises). The study compares two types of physical exercise in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized single-blind controlled trial comparing hydrotherapy treatment to land-based rehabilitation treatment in 34 PD patients. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a pilot RCT where 17 PD participants were randomized to Qigong exercise (n=8) or sham Qigong (n=9). Qigong is a mind-body physical exercise. The study compares exercise to a control condition in adults with PD. Meets selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper describing a risk-of-bias assessment tool for systematic reviews. It is not an RCT and does not involve any exercise intervention or PD patients.

This is a double-blind RCT where 130 PD patients were randomly assigned to aerobic exercise on a home trainer (n=65) or stretching as active control (n=65). Both are physical activities. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an RCT where 62 PD participants were randomly assigned to Argentine Tango program or control group (no intervention). Tango dancing is a physical exercise. The study compares exercise to a control group in adults with PD. Meets selection criteria.
This is an animal study using MPTP-lesioned mice, not human adults with PD. While it examines exercise effects, the population criterion (adults with PD) is not met.
This appears to be a historical review article discussing the natural history of parkinsonism. It is not an RCT and does not involve any exercise intervention.

This is a randomized, assessor-blinded study where 32 PD patients were assigned to Turo (hybrid qigong dancing) or waiting-list control. Turo is a physical exercise/dance intervention. The study compares exercise to a control group in adults with PD. Meets selection criteria.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study for measuring quality of life in PD patients. It is not an RCT and does not involve any physical exercise intervention.

This is described as a 'controlled clinical study' but does not explicitly state randomization was used. More importantly, the intervention is 'behavioral treatment' which is not clearly a physical exercise intervention. The control received 'nonspecific psychological treatment'. Does not meet the physical exercise criterion.

This is an RCT where 40 PD participants were randomly divided into balance training (BT) or resistance training (RT) groups. Both are physical exercise interventions being compared in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

While this is a cluster-RCT, it compares a care delivery model (ParkinsonNet network) to usual care, not specific types of physical exercise. The intervention is about how physiotherapy is organized and delivered, not about comparing exercise types. Does not meet the selection criteria.

This study compares Argentine tango to traditional strength/flexibility exercise in individuals with PD (and healthy elderly controls). The PD subgroup (n=19 per group) received either tango or traditional exercise. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets selection criteria for the PD population.
This is an observational population-based cohort study examining mortality predictors in parkinsonism/PD. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any physical exercise intervention.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of exercise therapies for PD, not a primary RCT. Secondary studies do not meet the inclusion criteria for this review.
This is a randomized clinical trial comparing a high-intensity agility exercise program to a no physical intervention control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a randomized clinical trial comparing Nintendo Wii alone, conventional exercises alone, and their combination in adults with PD. Multiple exercise interventions compared.
This is a randomized controlled trial evaluating a 6-month minimally supervised exercise program targeting leg strength, balance, and freezing vs control in people with PD.
This describes a software tool (robvis) for visualizing risk-of-bias assessments. It is not a clinical study and does not involve physical exercise intervention.
This is a 12-week crossover randomized trial evaluating interactive video-game-based exercise training vs no exercise control in older adults with mild-to-moderate PD.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study (PDQ-39). It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any physical exercise intervention.
This is a pilot randomized study comparing Global Postural Reeducation (GPR) physical therapy program to control in PD patients. GPR is a physical exercise/therapy intervention.
This is a randomized controlled trial evaluating 24-week resistance training program vs control in elderly people with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper describing graph-theoretical methods for network meta-analysis. It is not a clinical RCT and does not involve physical exercise intervention.
This is a single-blinded randomized controlled trial evaluating 12-week Tai Chi exercise vs no intervention control in people with PD. Tai Chi is a physical exercise intervention.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing high-intensity treadmill training, low-intensity exercise, and zero-intensity education control in early PD patients. Multiple exercise intensities compared.

This is a randomized controlled trial of a group-based music intervention. While music can be therapeutic, this appears to be primarily a music listening/intervention study rather than a physical exercise intervention. Does not meet the physical exercise criterion.
This is a randomized pilot study comparing multidisciplinary intensive rehabilitation treatment (MIRT) including physical exercise to drug-only control in early PD patients over 2 years.
This is an epidemiological analysis of neurological disease burden in Europe from the Global Burden of Disease Study. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any physical exercise intervention.
This is a single-blind randomized controlled trial evaluating PD-WEBB (Parkinson's disease-weight bearing exercise for better balance) training vs control in people with PD.
This is a randomized trial comparing Argentine tango, American ballroom (waltz/foxtrot), and no intervention control in people with PD. Both dance types are physical exercise interventions.
This is a randomized controlled crossover trial comparing aerobic training to Qigong (a Chinese medical exercise) in advanced PD patients. Both are physical exercise interventions.
This is a Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of physiotherapy interventions in PD. It is a secondary study, not a primary RCT.

This is a randomized clinical trial (ensaio clínico randomizado) comparing two types of physical exercise (Nordic walking vs free walking) in 33 people with Parkinson's disease. Meets all inclusion criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.

Prospective single-blind randomized clinical trial with 154 participants comparing three groups: RAS-supported multimodal balance training, regular multimodal balance training, and control (education program). Physical exercise interventions compared in adults with PD.

Randomized controlled trial with 54 patients comparing incremental speed-dependent treadmill training (21 patients) vs control group (10 patients with outcome data). Physical exercise intervention in adults with idiopathic PD.

This is a systematic review (Cochrane review), not a primary RCT. The abstract states 'We included 8 trials' indicating this is a review of other studies, not an original trial itself. Does not meet the RCT design criterion.

Randomized trial with 20 patients divided into control and experimental groups. Experimental group performed water-walking with dual-tasks for 4 weeks. Physical exercise intervention in adults with PD.

Randomized controlled feasibility study with 20 participants comparing high-intensity interval training vs waiting list control. Physical exercise intervention in adults with idiopathic PD. Feasibility RCTs are eligible.

This appears to be an observational/analytical study rather than an RCT. The abstract describes cohorts undergoing underwater or land-based training but does not mention randomization. Study design unclear/not explicitly RCT.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The abstract states 'From 1,130 trials, 19 relevant studies...were selected' indicating this reviews other studies. Does not meet RCT design criterion.

Comparative prospective randomized single-blinded clinical trial with 67 patients comparing three types of physical exercise: higher-intensity treadmill, lower-intensity treadmill, and stretching/resistance exercises. Meets all criteria.
This is a review article discussing pharmacological treatments (levodopa formulations, adenosine A2A antagonists, etc.), not a physical exercise RCT. Wrong study design and wrong intervention type.
Randomized controlled trial with 90 participants comparing Irish set dancing intervention vs usual care. Dance is a form of physical exercise. Meets all inclusion criteria.
This is an observational cross-sectional study evaluating nonmotor symptoms (anxiety, depression, fatigue, sleep disturbance) in 99 PD patients. No intervention, no randomization. Wrong study design.

Title indicates investigation of Health Qigong (physical exercise) effects on PD symptoms. Abstract is truncated but mentions 54 moderate PD patients. Conservative approach: include pending full text review to confirm RCT design.

RCT with 210 participants comparing progressive resistance strength training + falls prevention education, movement strategy training + falls prevention education, vs life-skills information control. Physical exercise interventions in adults with PD.
Open-label randomized controlled trial with 40 patients comparing Ai Chi (aquatic exercise) vs land-based exercise control. Physical exercise intervention in adults with mild-moderate PD.
Prospective randomized controlled study with 13 participants comparing dance/movement therapy vs psychoeducational support group. Dance is physical exercise. Pilot RCTs are eligible.
Randomized cross-over trial with 22 patients comparing physiotherapy programme with cueing and movement strategies vs no treatment. Physical exercise/rehabilitation intervention in adults with PD.

Pilot prospective single-blind randomized clinical trial with 35 patients in Hoehn & Yahr stage 4 comparing multimodal balance training with vs without rhythmical auditory stimuli. Physical exercise intervention in adults with advanced PD.
This is a review article ('This Review provides an overview...'). Discusses previously published reviews and makes recommendations. Not a primary RCT. Wrong study design.

This is a secondary analysis of data from a previously conducted RCT (the same trial as study 182). The abstract states 'A secondary analysis was conducted on a large randomized controlled trial'. Not a primary RCT; would result in double-counting participants.
RCT comparing rehabilitation exercise intervention to routine care (control group) in hospitalized PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares exercise to control.
Pilot RCT comparing Tango, Waltz/Foxtrot, Tai Chi to No Intervention in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares different exercise types to control.
Explicitly stated RCT comparing progressive resistance exercise to stretching/balance/strengthening program in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
RCT comparing Wuqinxi exercise to stretching in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
Neuropathological study examining brain tissue patterns of neuronal loss. Not an RCT, not an exercise intervention study.
RCT comparing curved-walking training to general exercise training in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
Clinimetric validation study of a rating scale. Not an RCT, not an exercise intervention study.
Cross-sectional observational study comparing PD patients to healthy controls. Not an RCT, not an exercise intervention study.
Prospective controlled trial comparing tango, treadmill walking, and stretching in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares multiple exercise types.
Review article on epidemiology and risk factors. Not an RCT, not an exercise intervention study.
RCT comparing adapted resistance training with instability to traditional motor rehabilitation in PD patients with freezing of gait. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
RCT comparing aerobic exercise, goal-based exercise, and control in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares exercise types to control.
RCT comparing balance training to general physical exercises in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
RCT comparing corrective exercise with balance pad, without balance pad, and control in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares exercise types to control.
RCT comparing water-based therapy to land-based therapy in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
RCT comparing Nordic walking to free walking in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.

RCT comparing intensive inpatient physical therapy (treadmill and stabilometric platform) to pharmacological treatment with generic home exercise in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares exercise intervention to control.
RCT comparing mindfulness yoga to stretching and resistance training in PD patients. Meets criteria as it compares two exercise types.
Review article about deep brain stimulation. Not an RCT, not an exercise intervention study.
Diagnostic criteria document. Not an RCT, not an exercise intervention study.

Randomized controlled trial comparing gait and step perturbation training (physical exercise intervention) to a control group in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, appropriate comparator.

This is a psychometric reliability study of a questionnaire (NFOG-Q), not a randomized controlled trial of physical exercise. No exercise intervention is tested; the study compares patient and carer ratings of freezing of gait. Does not meet the RCT criterion.

Randomized single-blind controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions: treadmill with music cueing, treadmill without music, and home walking. All are physical exercise interventions in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized comparative study comparing three physical exercise interventions: LSVT BIG (intensive high-amplitude movement training), Nordic Walking, and domestic nonsupervised exercises. All are physical exercise types in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized controlled study comparing three exercise/physiotherapy interventions: LSVT BIG, intensive physiotherapy, and conventional physiotherapy. All are physical exercise interventions in adults with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized controlled trial comparing virtual reality rehabilitation to conventional rehabilitation in adults with PD. Both interventions involve physical exercise/rehabilitation components. Meets all selection criteria.

Prospective crossover randomized trial comparing body weight-supported treadmill training to conventional physical therapy in adults with PD. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets all selection criteria.

Quasi-randomized trial comparing exercise therapy (1-hour sessions 4x/week) to control (pharmacological therapy only) in adults with PD. While quasi-randomized rather than fully randomized, following conservative screening principles, this should be included for full-text review to confirm randomization method.
Randomized controlled pilot trial comparing home-based treadmill training to usual care in adults with mild PD. Physical exercise intervention with appropriate control. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized controlled study comparing Dance Therapy (psychotherapeutic movement intervention involving physical exercise) to a support group in adults with PD. Dance therapy involves physical movement/exercise. Meets selection criteria.

Randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions: flexibility/balance/function exercise, supervised aerobic exercise, and home-based exercise in adults with PD. All are physical exercise interventions. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, not a primary randomized controlled trial itself. The selection criteria specify inclusion of RCTs, not reviews of RCTs. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Randomized controlled trial comparing a home exercise program (strength training, movement strategy training) to non-specific life skills training in adults with PD. The intervention includes physical exercise components. Meets all selection criteria.
